newsitem.title: USA: West Virginia has $18 million surplus for FY 1997.
newsitem.headline: West Virginia has $18 million surplus for FY 1997.

text.p: West Virginia revenue collections totalled $2.42 billion for the year ended Tuesday, exceeding projections by $16.8 million, according to a report by State Auditor Glen Gainer III.

State agencies must return leftover money to the state treasury at the end of July, which should add another $1 million to $1.5 million, giving West Virgina a surplus of about $18 million for the year.

By law, half of the surplus must go into the state's Rainy Day Fund, which had a $57.4 million balance at the end of May. The Legislature has already appropriated another $8 million of the surplus on a contingency basis.

The yearly boost in revenues came even though June receipts were $25 million below estimates, the report said. Personal income tax collections were off by $20.4 milion for the month but only by $810,000 for the year.
Consumer sales taxes were also off for June, by about $3.8 million.
